info.label: Columbia
info.desc: Random Access Memories is the fourth and final studio album by French electronic music duo Daft Punk. It was released by Daft Life under exclusive license to Columbia Records on May 17, 2013 in Australia, May 20, 2013 in the United Kingdom and on May 21, 2013 in the United States. Work started on the record concurrently with the Tron: Legacy score, without a clear plan as to what its structure would be. Shortly after Daft Punk signed with Columbia, a gradual promotional rollout began for the album including billboards, television advertising and a web series. Random Access Memories pays .

podcast.body: After an eight-year gap between albums, Random Access Memories involved collaborations with Giorgio Moroder (pioneering synth-dance producer), Nile Rodgers of Chic (a personal hero who also produced Bowie's Let's Dance), Julian Casablancas of the Strokes, songwriter Paul Williams, Canadian pianist Chilly Gonzalez, Panda Bear from Animal Collective, jazz bassist Nathan East, and producer Todd Edwards among others. Influences studied included Fleetwood Mac, The Cars, Steely Dan, the Eagles, the Doobie Brothers, Michael Jackson, and Pink Floyd's Dark Side of the Moon. They recorded too much material and briefly considered a four-disc box set before cutting everything to 74 minutes (just under a CD's maximum capacity). Released May 17, 2013, it became their only number one album in North America. "Get Lucky" hit number one in 30 countries and became one of the biggest-selling digital singles of all time. The album won multiple Grammys in 2014. "Random access memories became the only number one Daft Punk album in North America."

podcast.body: This album on vinyl, specifically described as two 100-gram slabs, retailed for $45, serving as an example of the "ridiculous prices" that record labels began charging for new vinyl, which potentially threatens the format's resurrection. "I have a copy of Death Punk's random access memories album on two 100-day Graham Slabs of vinyl that retailed for $45."

podcast.body: This album, described as the "robotic French duo's most retro sounding LP," took its first Album of the Year Grammy for Electronic Dance Music in 2014. It was also noted as their "final album" at the time of the recording. "Electronic Dance Music took its first album of the Year when Draft Punk won for their final album Random Access Memories."
